q: A Class II hazardous (classified) location is one where the hazard is from:
explain: Class I = flammable gases/vapors/liquids; Class II = combustible dust; Class III = ignitable fibers and flyings.

q: A location where ignitable concentrations of flammable gases exist under normal operating conditions is:
explain: Division 1 = present under normal operation (or frequently due to maintenance/leakage). Division 2 = only under abnormal conditions, normally confined in closed systems.

q: In a Class I, Division 1 location, a conduit seal entering an enclosure containing arcing devices must be installed within how far of the enclosure?
explain: Within 18 in. (450 mm), with only explosionproof fittings between the seal and the enclosure.

q: In a major repair garage with no mechanical ventilation, the space up to what height above the floor is classified as Class I, Division 2?
explain: Up to 18 in. above the floor across the whole floor area. With ventilation providing at least 4 air changes per hour (or the equivalent), the area may be unclassified.

q: Each patient bed location in a general care (Category 2) space must be supplied by at least:
choices: Two branch circuits: one from the critical branch and one from the normal system
Three branch circuits from the life-safety branch
explain: At least two branch circuits, one from the critical branch and one from the normal system (or two critical-branch circuits under conditions).

q: Minimum receptacle counts at patient bed locations are:
explain: General care (Category 2): at least 8 receptacles. Critical care (Category 1): at least 14. All must be hospital grade and marked.

q: General-purpose receptacles near a permanently installed pool must be located at least how far from the inside walls of the pool?
explain: Not less than 6 ft. Pump-motor receptacles: 6 to 10 ft, single, locking, grounding, GFCI. All 125 V, 15/20 A receptacles within 20 ft must be GFCI-protected.

q: The equipotential bonding grid around a permanently installed pool uses a solid copper conductor not smaller than:
explain: 8 AWG solid copper (insulated, covered or bare), bonding the perimeter surface, metallic parts, shell steel, and equipment.

q: A luminaire mounted in a pool wall must have the top of its lens at least how far below the normal water level?
explain: 18 in. (450 mm) below normal water level, unless listed and identified for use at lesser depths (never less than 4 in.).

q: The maximum current of a PV source circuit is calculated as:
choices: 100% of the sum of parallel-connected module short-circuit currents
125% of the sum of parallel-connected module short-circuit currents
explain: 125% of Isc for the source circuit (accounts for irradiance above STC). Conductors are then sized at 125% of that maximum current (690.8(B)) — the familiar 156% net.

q: Under the rapid shutdown rules, controlled conductors located outside the array boundary must be reduced to not more than how many volts within 30 seconds of initiation?
explain: Outside the array boundary (and more than 1 ft from it): 30 V within 30 seconds. Inside the boundary: 80 V within 30 seconds, or a listed PV hazard-control system.

q: The maximum PV system DC voltage for a series string is based on the rated open-circuit voltage corrected for:
explain: Voc rises as temperature falls, so the lowest expected ambient temperature (or manufacturer coefficients / Table 690.7(A)) governs maximum voltage.

q: An emergency system's power source must be available to the loads within how many seconds of normal supply failure?
explain: Emergency (Art. 700): 10 s. Legally required standby (Art. 701): 60 s. Optional standby (Art. 702): no time requirement.

q: A 200 A busbar panel with a 200 A main breaker will have a PV inverter breaker connected at the opposite end of the bus. Using the 120% rule, the largest inverter breaker permitted is:
explain: 120% × 200 A = 240 A total; 240 − 200 (main) = 40 A inverter OCPD, with the inverter breaker at the opposite end from the main and a warning label.

q: Each commercial building or occupancy accessible to pedestrians must have at least one outlet for a sign or outline lighting at each entrance, supplied by a branch circuit rated at least:
explain: A 20 A branch circuit that supplies no other load, within 50 ft of the entrance (2020 relaxed the exact location).

q: A legally required standby system must have its alternate source available within:
choices: Any time set by the AHJ
explain: 60 seconds for legally required standby; 10 seconds for emergency systems.

q: The receptacle for a permanently installed pool's pump motor, where located near the pool, must be:
choices: Within 3 ft of the pool for convenience
Between 6 ft and 10 ft from the inside walls, single, locking and grounding type, GFCI protected
explain: 6–10 ft, locking/grounding single receptacle, GFCI-protected.

q: The PV system disconnecting means must be:
choices: Readily accessible and marked 'PV SYSTEM DISCONNECT' (or equivalent)
explain: Readily accessible, permanently marked, and (where the line and load terminals may be energized in the open position) carrying a warning label.

q: In agricultural buildings, 15 and 20 A, 125 V receptacles installed in areas with an equipotential plane, outdoors, or in damp/wet locations require:
explain: GFCI protection for receptacles in those agricultural-building locations and in dirt-confinement areas for livestock.

q: A Class 2 circuit is best described as one that:
choices: Is power-limited by its listed Class 2 source so it poses an acceptable shock and fire risk
Must be installed in rigid metal conduit
explain: Class 2 (e.g., thermostat and doorbell circuits) is limited at the source. Class 2 conductors are kept separate from power conductors (725.136).
